// THE ENGINE, read before anything else runs (a var, so early callers never // hit a TDZ). WebKit — Safari, and the Playwright WebKit shell under any UA // (meet.js --profile phone wears an Android Chrome UA) — keeps // navigator.vendor 'Apple Computer, Inc.'; Chromium says 'Google Inc.', // Firefox ''. The UA test is the fallback for an engine that hides it. var WEBKIT_ENGINE = (() => { try { const ua = navigator.userAgent || ''; if ((navigator.vendor || '').indexOf('Apple') === 0) return true; return /AppleWebKit/.test(ua) && !/Chrome|Chromium|CriOS|Edg\/|FxiOS|Android/.test(ua); } catch (e) { return false; } })(); /* * GifOS Meeting — a SYSTEM app (first-party page, not a sandboxed GIF app). * Sandboxed apps have WebRTC deliberately neutered and no network, and camera * permission can't be granted to an opaque origin — so live media has to run * at this trusted level. The desktop icon is still a real GIF; its manifest * says { system: "video" } and the runtime routes it here. * * Topology: full mesh over a PERMANENT, HOST-LESS ROOM. The room IS its URL: * nobody owns it, so nobody's departure (including the creator's) can break * it — whoever opens the link joins whoever is there, forever. The relay's * "mesh" role introduces browsers and carries ONLY SDP/ICE; it hard-throttles * anything heavier, so media cannot fall back to it — P2P or nothing. * * Resilience, in order of likely failure: * - relay socket dies (phone locks, network blips) → auto-reconnect with * backoff, kicked instantly on visibility/online; live P2P links stay up * - a P2P link degrades → the deterministic initiator (larger peer id) * re-offers with an ICE restart until it heals * - a peer truly leaves → their tile is dropped only after a grace period, * so a phone-lock never kills a tile that's about to come back * - the camera dies in a background tab → re-acquired and re-plugged into * every link when the tab returns * - no camera permission at all → you still JOIN (view-only) instead of * being locked out */ // The scripts above are deferred so they fetch together. This assigns the // starter. The module after this script runs it once those libraries have // executed, and before DOMContentLoaded. window.__startMeet = function () { // THE HOST'S FACTS the meeting asks about (GifOS.host): whether the page is hidden from its person (a background // tab); the origin of the page that frames this one (a meeting session in about:srcdoc has none of its own); whether // this browser can hold a meeting at all (the preflight gate runs `f` only then); the page's own scripts in page order // and loading one again (the load gate); the size of the screen it draws on. A browser page answers from its // document; a host with no screen brings its own answers. if (!GifOS.host) GifOS.host = { hidden: () => document.hidden, parentOrigin: () => { try { if (window.parent && window.parent !== window && window.parent.location && window.parent.location.origin) return window.parent.location.origin; } catch (e) {} return ''; }, whenSupported: (f) => { const P = window.GifOSPreflight; if (P && typeof P.whenSupported === 'function') P.whenSupported(f); else f(); }, scriptOrder: () => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('script[src]')).map((el) => { try { return new URL(el.src, location.href).pathname.replace(/^\//, ''); } catch (e) { return ''; } }), loadScript: (src) => new Promise((res) => { const el = document.createElement('script'); el.async = false; el.src = src; el.onload = () => res(true); /* a failure is its error event; a size of 0 is a Safari 304, not a missing body (see #gifos-load-gate) */ el.onerror = () => { el.remove(); res(false); }; document.head.appendChild(el); }), viewport: () => ({ w: window.innerWidth, h: window.innerHeight }), }; GifOS.core.startPage(); };
